definition: A controllable braking function used to reduce train speed during normal operation; the exercise controller represents graduated requests with B1, B2 and B3.
A safety braking function intended for situations requiring urgent deceleration, distinct from ordinary service braking.
Restoring an emergency braking system to a releasable state under the applicable train and operator procedures, after its cause has been addressed.
A device in a pneumatic friction-braking system in which air pressure can operate the mechanical brake gear.
A pneumatic line used in certain train braking arrangements to convey pressure changes or brake commands along the train.
Kilopascal, a unit of pressure used on some train brake-system gauges.
The distance a train travels while decelerating from a specified speed to a stop; affected by speed, adhesion, gradient and other conditions.
